plan: In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins (when the highest competing bid is below my value). Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value if rivals’ bids exceed it. There’s no useful history (single round), and values are redrawn independently. With value $19, bidding 19 ensures I win exactly when it’s profitable and pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing nonnegative surplus. Ties, if any, are resolved randomly without changing this logic.

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning when another’s value exceeds yours and paying above your value. With values redrawn each round and a 0.1 grid, there’s no advantage to shading or tie tactics. To maximize expected profit this round (and long run), bid exactly your valuation of 44. ]

[ Second-price sealed-bid with independent private values: truth-telling is a weakly dominant strategy. With rational opponents, they will also bid their values. Bidding my value 43 maximizes expected profit: I win exactly when my value exceeds both others’ values and pay the second-highest bid (their value), yielding profit 43 − max(other bids). Shading risks losing when I’d profit; overbidding risks negative profit if I win when my value is not highest. Bids allowed in $0.1 increments; 43 is valid. ]
